summary: The firstborn of a donkey must be redeemed, but only if it belongs fully to a Jew. If a non-Jew owns any part of it, or if it belongs to Kohanim or Levi'im, it does not have the halachos of a bechor.

chunks.en: Someone who buys the unborn baby of a non-Jew's donkey,
chunks.st: With regard to one who purchases the fetus of a donkey that belongs to a gentile,

chunks.he: וְהַמּוֹכֵר לוֹ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי,
chunks.en: or sells his donkey's unborn baby to a non-Jew, even though he is not allowed to,
chunks.st: and one who sells the fetus of his donkey to a gentile although he is not permitted to sell a large animal to a gentile,

words.note: Chazal did not let a Jew sell a big work animal to a non-Jew.

chunks.en: or becomes partners with a non-Jew in a donkey,
chunks.st: and one who enters into a partnership with
chunks.stMore: a gentile in ownership of a donkey or its fetus,

chunks.en: or takes a donkey from a non-Jew to care for it and share the babies,
chunks.st: and one who receives a donkey from
chunks.stMore: a gentile in order to care for it in exchange for partnership in its offspring,

chunks.en: or gives his donkey to a non-Jew to care for it in that way,
chunks.st: and one who gives his donkey to a gentile in receivership,

chunks.en: in all of these cases, the baby donkey is not a bechor.
chunks.st: in all of these cases the donkeys are exempt from the obligations of firstborn status,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they do not have firstborn status and are not redeemed,

words.note: A bechor is a firstborn. A firstborn donkey must be redeemed by giving a lamb to a Kohen.

chunks.en: Because the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "the firstborns in Yisrael," but not those of others.
chunks.st: “I sanctified to Me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal” (Numbers 3:13), indicating that the mitzva is incumbent upon the Jewish people, but not upon others.
chunks.stMore: If the firstborn belongs even partially to a gentile, it does not have firstborn status.

chunks.en: Kohanim and Levi'im do not have to redeem a firstborn donkey; we learn it from a kal vachomer:
chunks.st: Priests and Levites are exempt from the obligation to redeem a firstborn donkey; this is derived from an a fortiori
chunks.stMore: inference: In the wilderness the firstborn were redeemed in exchange for the Levites, as it is stated: “Take the Levites in exchange for all the firstborn among the children of Israel and the animal of the Levites in exchange for their animals” (Numbers 3:45).

words.note: A kal vachomer is a proof that goes from an easier case to a harder case.

chunks.en: In the midbar, the Levi'im took the place of the firstborns of the rest of Yisrael,
chunks.st: If the priests and Levites rendered exempt the firstborn children and donkeys of the Israelites in the wilderness from being counted firstborns,

chunks.en: so surely they should free their own firstborns.
chunks.st: it is only logical that the priests and the Levites should render the firstborn of their own donkeys exempt from being counted firstborns.

summary: Only a donkey born from a donkey is a bechor. A baby that looks like a different animal is kosher or not kosher depending on its mother, and a fish found inside another fish is judged by what kind of fish it is.

chunks.en: A cow that gave birth to a baby that looks like a donkey,
chunks.st: A cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts

chunks.en: or a donkey that gave birth to a baby that looks like a horse,
chunks.st: and a donkey that gave birth to a horse of sorts

chunks.en: the baby is not a bechor,
chunks.st: are exempt from their offspring being counted a firstborn,

chunks.en: because the Torah says "firstborn of a donkey, firstborn of a donkey,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 13:13); “and the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 34:20).

chunks.en: two times,
chunks.st: The Torah states this halakha twice,

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הַיּוֹלֵד חֲמוֹר וְהַנּוֹלָד חֲמוֹר.
chunks.en: to teach that the mother must be a donkey and the baby must be a donkey.
chunks.st: indicating that one is not obligated unless both the birth mother is a donkey and the animal born is a donkey.

chunks.en: And what about eating them?
chunks.st: And what is the halakhic status of offspring that are unlike the mother animal with regard to their consumption?

chunks.he: בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה,
chunks.en: A kosher animal that gave birth to a baby that looks like a non-kosher animal,
chunks.st: In the case of a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher animal of sorts,

chunks.en: may be eaten.
chunks.st: its consumption is permitted.

chunks.en: And a non-kosher animal that gave birth to a baby that looks like a kosher animal,
chunks.st: And in the case of a non-kosher animal that gave birth to a kosher animal of sorts,

chunks.en: may not be eaten,
chunks.st: its consumption is prohibited.

chunks.en: because what comes out of a non-kosher animal is non-kosher,
chunks.st: This is because that which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher

chunks.en: and what comes out of a kosher animal is kosher.
chunks.st: and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher.

chunks.en: A non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish:
chunks.st: In the case of a non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish,

chunks.en: the kosher fish may be eaten.
chunks.st: consumption of the kosher fish is permitted.

chunks.en: And a kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish:
chunks.st: And in the case of a kosher fish that swallowed a non-kosher fish,

chunks.en: the non-kosher fish may not be eaten,
chunks.st: consumption of the non-kosher fish is prohibited

chunks.en: because it did not grow inside the kosher fish.
chunks.st: due to the fact that the host fish is not the place of its development.

summary: When donkeys that never gave birth before have more than one baby, and we don't know which came first, the Kohen gets a lamb only if a male surely came first.

chunks.en: A donkey that never gave birth before
chunks.st: In the case of a female donkey that had not previously given birth

chunks.en: and now gave birth to two males:
chunks.st: and now gave birth to two male
chunks.stMore: offspring, as there is no doubt that one of them is firstborn, its owner

chunks.en: he gives one lamb to the Kohen.
chunks.st: gives one lamb to the priest in redemption of that firstborn.

chunks.en: A male and a female, and we don't know which came first:
chunks.st: If it gave birth to a male and a female and it is not known which was born first,

chunks.en: he sets aside one lamb and keeps it for himself.
chunks.st: he designates one lamb as firstborn in case the male was born first. Nevertheless, since it is merely a monetary debt to the priest, the burden of proof rests upon the claimant, in this case the priest. Due to that uncertainty, the priest can offer no proof and the owner keeps the lamb for himself.

chunks.en: Two donkeys that never gave birth before
chunks.st: If an individual has two donkeys, and both of his two donkeys had not previously given birth

chunks.en: and they gave birth to two males:
chunks.st: and they now gave birth to two males, one each,

chunks.en: he gives two lambs to the Kohen.
chunks.st: the owner gives two lambs to the priest.

chunks.en: A male and a female,
chunks.st: If they together gave birth to a male and a female

chunks.en: or two males and a female:
chunks.st: or to two males and a female,

chunks.en: he gives one lamb to the Kohen.
chunks.st: he gives one lamb to the priest, as one of the males is certainly a firstborn.

chunks.en: Two females and a male,
chunks.st: If they together gave birth to two females and a male

chunks.en: or two males and two females:
chunks.st: or to two males and two females,

chunks.en: the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: the priest receives nothing, as perhaps the two firstborn were females.

summary: More cases of two donkeys giving birth. The mishnah teaches which lambs may be used to redeem a firstborn donkey, and that a lamb kept because of a doubt belongs fully to the owner.

chunks.en: If one donkey had given birth before,
chunks.st: If one of his donkeys had previously given birth

chunks.en: and one had not given birth before,
chunks.st: and one had not previously given birth

chunks.en: and they gave birth to two males:
chunks.st: and they now together gave birth to two males,

chunks.en: he gives one lamb to the Kohen.
chunks.st: the owner gives one lamb to the priest as redemption for the firstborn male.

chunks.en: A male and a female:
chunks.st: If they together gave birth to a male and a female

chunks.en: he sets aside one lamb for himself.
chunks.st: he designates one lamb for himself,
chunks.stMore: as it is uncertain whether or not the male was a firstborn and the burden of proof rests upon the claimant. From where is it derived that the firstborn of a donkey is redeemed with a lamb? It is derived from a verse,

chunks.en: As the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a seh,"
chunks.st: “And you shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb [seh]” (Exodus 34:20).

words.note: A seh is a lamb or a young goat.

chunks.en: from the sheep or from the goats,
chunks.st: The owner may give a lamb either from sheep or from goats;

chunks.en: a male or a female,
chunks.st: from males or females,

chunks.en: big or small,
chunks.st: from older or younger animals,

chunks.en: without a blemish or with a blemish.
chunks.st: and from unblemished or blemished animals.

words.note: A mum, something wrong with the body.

chunks.en: And he may redeem with it many times.
chunks.st: If the priest returns the lamb to the owner, he may redeem firstborn donkeys with it many times.
chunks.stMore: In a case where he designates a lamb due to uncertainty and keeps it for himself, it is his in every sense. Consequently,

chunks.en: The lamb he kept for himself goes into the pen to be counted for ma'aser,
chunks.st: it enters the pen in order to be tithed
chunks.stMore: with the other non-sacred animals (see Leviticus 27:32),

words.note: Every tenth animal is given as ma'aser.

chunks.en: and if it dies,
chunks.st: and if it dies,

chunks.en: he may use it.
chunks.st: one may derive benefit from its carcass.

summary: Which animals may not be used to redeem a firstborn donkey, and what a Kohen must do if he is given the donkey itself.

chunks.en: We do not redeem a firstborn donkey with a calf,
chunks.st: One may not redeem a firstborn donkey, neither with a calf,

chunks.en: nor with a wild animal,
chunks.st: nor with an undomesticated animal,

chunks.en: nor with a shechted animal,
chunks.st: nor with a slaughtered animal,

chunks.en: nor with a treifah,
chunks.st: nor with a tereifa,

words.note: An animal with a deadly injury or sickness.

chunks.en: nor with a mixed animal, half sheep and half goat,
chunks.st: nor with a hybrid of a sheep and a goat,

chunks.en: nor with a koy.
chunks.st: nor with a koy,
chunks.stMore: which is an animal with regard to which it is uncertain whether it is domesticated or undomesticated.

words.note: An animal that we are not sure is wild or tame.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar allows the mixed animal,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Eliezer deems it permitted to redeem a firstborn donkey with a hybrid of a sheep and a goat,

chunks.en: because it is a seh,
chunks.st: because it is a lamb, i.e., that hybrid has the status of a lamb,

chunks.en: but forbids the koy, because it is a doubt.
chunks.st: but prohibits redeeming it with a koy, because its status is uncertain.

chunks.en: If he gave the donkey itself to the Kohen,
chunks.st: If one gave the firstborn donkey to a priest,

chunks.en: the Kohen may not keep it
chunks.st: the priest may not keep it

chunks.en: until he sets aside a lamb in its place.
chunks.st: unless he first designates a lamb in its stead for redemption.

summary: What happens if the lamb set aside to redeem a firstborn donkey dies, or if the donkey dies first.

chunks.en: Someone set aside a lamb to redeem a firstborn donkey, and the lamb died.
chunks.st: In the case of one who designates a lamb for the redemption of a firstborn donkey and the lamb dies,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: he is responsible for it and must give another,
chunks.st: The owner bears financial responsibility
chunks.stMore: and must give the priest another lamb in its place.

chunks.en: like the five sela'im for redeeming a son.
chunks.st: This is like the case of the five sela for redemption of a firstborn son,
chunks.stMore: where if the money is lost before one gives it to the priest, he must give the priest another five sela.

words.note: A sela is a silver coin.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he is not responsible for it,
chunks.st: The owner does not bear financial responsibility.

chunks.en: like money used to redeem ma'aser sheni.
chunks.st: This is like the case of money designated for redemption of second-tithe
chunks.stMore: produce, where once the owner designates the money for redemption, the produce is desanctified.

words.note: Second tithe, food eaten in Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok told
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok testified

chunks.en: about a lamb for redeeming a firstborn donkey that died,
chunks.st: about a lamb designated for redemption of a firstborn donkey that died,

chunks.en: that the Kohen gets nothing here.
chunks.st: that the priest has nothing here,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in such a case, as the firstborn donkey has already been redeemed, and the owner no longer bears financial responsibility for the dead lamb, in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis.

chunks.en: If the firstborn donkey died,
chunks.st: If after the lamb was designated, the firstborn donkey died,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it must be buried, and the owner may use the lamb.
chunks.st: The donkey must be buried, and the owner is permitted to derive benefit from the lamb.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: it does not need to be buried,
chunks.st: It does not need to be buried,

chunks.en: and the lamb goes to the Kohen.
chunks.st: and the lamb is given to the priest.

summary: If a person does not want to redeem a firstborn donkey, he must break its neck. The mishnah lists mitzvos where one choice comes before another.

chunks.en: If he did not want to redeem it,
chunks.st: If one did not wish to redeem the firstborn donkey,

chunks.en: he breaks its neck from behind with a cleaver and buries it.
chunks.st: he breaks its neck from behind and buries it.

chunks.en: The mitzvah of redeeming comes before the mitzvah of breaking the neck,
chunks.st: The mitzva of redeeming the firstborn donkey takes precedence over the mitzva of breaking the neck,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck."
chunks.st: “If you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck”
chunks.stMore: (Exodus 13:13). The mishna proceeds to enumerate other mitzvot in which one option takes precedence over another.

words.en: and you shall break its neck

chunks.en: The mitzvah of yi'udah comes before the mitzvah of redeeming a Jewish maidservant,
chunks.st: The mitzva of designating a Hebrew maidservant to be betrothed to her master takes precedence over the mitzva of redeeming the maidservant from her master with money,

words.note: When the master marries the Jewish maidservant.

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “If she does not please her master,

chunks.en: "who did not marry her, then he shall let her be redeemed."
chunks.st: who has not betrothed her to himself, then he shall let her be redeemed” (Exodus 21:8).

chunks.en: The mitzvah of yibum comes before the mitzvah of chalitzah.
chunks.st: The mitzva of levirate marriage takes precedence over the mitzva of ḥalitza,
chunks.stMore: which dissolves the levirate bond, as it is stated: “And if the man does not wish to take his brother’s wife” (Deuteronomy 25:7). The mishna adds:

words.note: Marrying the widow of a brother who had no children.
A ceremony that frees the widow instead of yibum.

chunks.en: That was in the early days, when people did it for the sake of the mitzvah.
chunks.st: This was the case initially, when people would intend that their performance of levirate marriage be for the sake of the mitzva.

chunks.en: But now that people do not do it for the sake of the mitzvah,
chunks.st: But now that they do not intend that their performance of levirate marriage be for the sake of the mitzva,
chunks.stMore: but rather for reasons such as the beauty of the yevama or for financial gain,

chunks.he: אָמְרוּ מִצְוַת חֲלִיצָה קוֹדֶמֶת לְמִצְוַת יִבּוּם.
chunks.en: the Sages said that chalitzah comes before yibum.
chunks.st: the Sages said that the mitzva of ḥalitza takes precedence over the mitzva of levirate marriage.
chunks.stMore: With regard to a non-kosher animal that was consecrated to the Temple,

chunks.en: The mitzvah of buying back a hekdesh animal is first for its owner,
chunks.st: the mitzva of redemption by the owner who consecrated it

chunks.en: before any other person,
chunks.st: takes precedence over redemption by any other person,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And if it is of a non-kosher animal…

chunks.en: "And if it is not bought back, it shall be sold at its value."
chunks.st: and if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold according to your valuation” (Leviticus 27:27).
